newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister defends franc-mark parity - paper.
newsitem.headline: French minister defends franc-mark parity - paper.

text.p: French Trade Minister Yves Galland said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that trade flows between France and Germany showed that the French franc was correctly valued against the German mark.

He told the newspaper Figaro that a recent proposal by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for a lower franc was a bad idea. "We've always opposed competitive devaluations," Galland said, adding that recent gains in the U.S. dollar and Italian lira showed that "currencies cannot remain chronically undervalued".
As for the franc-mark parity, trade flows between the two countries suggest the level is right, he said.
France's share of the German market is 11 percent currently, compared with 10.8 percent of the west German market in 1980. "The parity therefore isn't handicapping France," he said.

In contrast, the dollar's weakness has been costly. "All our industries are suffering -- aeronautics, the arms industry, civilian contracts of all sorts. The dollar is effectively undervalued in relation to the fundamentals of the U.S. economy," he said.
As 63 percent of French trade is with other European countries, the creation of a single currency will reduce France's exposure to foreign exchange swings, he said.
"Creating monetary union...will shelter two-thirds of our trade from monetary dumping," he said.
